items.title: 🤖 TOP 10 AI NEWS
items.summary:
🤖 TOP 10 AI NEWS

1. 🚀 Anthropic Unveils Claude Fable 5.2 & Mythos 5.2

Anthropic reportedly launched its most powerful models yet, promising 30% faster output and improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision.

💰 Fable 5.2 pricing: $8 input / $40 output per million tokens.

Mythos 5.2 remains restricted to verified organisations in specialised programmes.

The launch comes as Anthropic prepares for a potentially historic IPO.

2. 🛡️ OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber: A Major Cybersecurity Leap

OpenAI’s new security-focused model reportedly identified:

• 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities

• 948 working privilege-escalation exploits

• 81 high-severity Firefox flaws

The system reportedly used approximately $1.2 million in API credits.

With a “Critical” cybersecurity capability rating, access is limited to approved defenders.

AI-assisted security research is entering a new era.

3. 💰 Anthropic’s IPO Reveals Explosive Growth — and Rising Losses

Anthropic’s updated IPO filing reportedly shows:

📈 Quarterly revenue: $17 billion

📊 Revenue growth: 47% quarter over quarter

📉 Operating loss: $567 million

Despite rapid growth, investors are questioning the timing of its IPO and a potential valuation as high as $1.5 trillion.

4. 🤖 Nvidia Reveals GR00T 2 Amid CEO Scrutiny

Nvidia reportedly showcased GR00T 2, a 2-billion-parameter robotics model that achieved first-attempt success on 71% of tested robotics tasks.

Meanwhile, its board reportedly opened an independent inquiry into allegations involving CEO Jensen Huang and foreign intelligence activity.

Nvidia says it has no evidence that company secrets were compromised.

The company remains central to both AI infrastructure and physical AI.

5. ⚡ OpenAI Plans Shared ChatGPT & Codex Usage Limits

Starting in December, OpenAI reportedly plans to introduce a shared token allowance across ChatGPT and Codex for Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers.

Instant chat would remain outside the shared allowance.

The proposed change reflects the growing convergence of AI chat, coding, and autonomous computer-use agents.

6. ⚖️ US Justice Department Creates a Super Intelligence Task Force

The US Department of Justice is establishing a specialised unit to coordinate AI-related prosecutions and address certain state AI laws.

AI misuse, national security, and regulatory enforcement are becoming increasingly important government priorities.

7. 📉 AI Stocks Lose $2.5 TRILLION as Data-Center Opposition Grows

AI-related stocks reportedly suffered a massive selloff, erasing approximately $2.5 trillion from the Nasdaq 100’s market value in one session.

Meanwhile, voters reportedly supported restrictions on data-center development in 40 of 41 local ballot measures.

The message is becoming clear: AI growth faces financial, environmental, and infrastructure challenges.

8. 🔥 Meta Launches Ultra-Cheap Muse Ember

Meta reportedly introduced Muse Ember, targeting high-volume AI workloads with aggressive pricing:

💰 Input: $0.10 per million tokens

💰 Output: $0.50 per million tokens

Meta also reportedly acquired Conductor, a platform designed to run multiple AI coding agents together.

The battle for affordable AI automation is intensifying.

9. 🎓 Google Changes AI Access for Schools

Google reportedly announced that Gemini and AI-powered Search features will be disabled by default for K–12 student accounts unless administrators enable them.

Meanwhile, Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash expands Google’s AI video capabilities, and Gemini 4 Carbon is being introduced to selected cybersecurity users.

Google is balancing rapid AI innovation with growing concerns about safety and access.

10. 🌍 Mistral Challenges Closed AI With Large 4

Mistral reportedly released Large 4, a 1-trillion-parameter open-weight model, under a modified MIT licence.

The release could give businesses more control over AI deployment, infrastructure, and costs.

#ArtificialIntelligence #AINews #OpenAI #Anthropic #ClaudeAI #ChatGPT

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Live online certificate brings AI expertise to finance professionals | Cornell Chronicle
items.summary: That philosophy is reflected in the curriculum, which progresses from AI foundations and tools to financial use cases, responsible AI, industry applications and leadership. Participants examine applications including investment research, credit risk, fraud detection, compliance, client engagement and operational efficiency, while also considering issues such as hallucinations, data security, regulation and governance. The program concludes by asking participants to identify opportunities for AI [...] The AI in Finance certificate, offered through eCornell as a collaboration between the Cornell Duffield College of Engineering and the Cornell SC Johnson College of Business, debuted in spring 2026 with 37 participants. Unlike many online certificate programs built primarily around prerecorded material, the program is taught live online, allowing participants to interact directly with Cornell faculty and industry practitioners. [...] Averbukh, who is also a professor of practice in the School of Operations Research and Information Engineering, said conversations with those practitioners increasingly turned toward artificial intelligence – first big data and predictive analytics, then machine learning and, more recently, generative and agentic AI.

items.title: Google AI policy forces decision for San Diego schools – NBC 7 San Diego
items.summary:
As districts consider their options, students are already seeing artificial intelligence become a more common part of everyday learning.

“I feel like I see a lot of people using AI now,” said Delilah Ortiz, a student at El Camino High School.

Some students believe the focus should be on establishing guidelines for AI use rather than banning the technology entirely. [...] San Diego County school districts face a January deadline to decide whether to opt in to Google's artificial intelligence features or lose access to the company's search engine, forcing educators to weigh the benefits of AI against concerns about student access to the technology. [...] Google plans to disable a range of AI-powered features, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search in January to give school districts more control over the technology students can access. However, districts that want to continue using Google Search will have to opt in to the AI features.

items.title: Military-made AI tool helped thwart World Cup bomb threat - Federal News Network
items.summary:
The 2026 World Cup brought more than six million spectators from around the world to more than 100 matches in 16 host cities in the U.S., Canada and Mexico over the course of two months, prompting a massive interagency effort to secure those sites using technologies like AI and drones. Two people were charged in connection with another bomb threat against FIFA during a World Cup match at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. [...] A military-made artificial intelligence tool helped law enforcement thwart a bomb threat at the FIFA World Cup in California this summer.

The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. Ryan Hetrick, who leads the Pentagon’s Generative AI Task Force, said Nov. 6 at an AI event in Washington. [...] Hetrick has become one of the military’s biggest — and busiest — evangelists for AI. The GenAI Task Force travels around the globe to sit down with troops on operations floors and in the field and find AI fixes for their most pressing problems.

items.title: Công nghệ gen tạo động lực đột phá cho ngành nông nghiệp
items.summary:
Giai đoạn 2026-2030, Việt Nam đặt mục tiêu xy dựng ít nhất 5 phòng thí nghiệm trọng điểm và 5 phòng thí nghiệm chuyên ngành hiện đại, tập trung vào công nghệ gen, công nghệ tế bào thực vật và động vật, vi sinh vật, thú y và chẩn đoán dịch bệnh. Mục tiêu đến năm 2035, tầm nhìn đến năm 2045 là làm chủ hoàn toàn công nghệ sinh học thế hệ mới và công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen để tạo ra các sản phẩm thương mại phục vụ thị trường trong nước và xuất khẩu. [...] Được xếp vào danh mục công nghệ chiến lược cấp quốc gia, công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen, đặc biệt là CRISPR/Cas, đang mở ra vận hội lớn để nông nghiệp Việt Nam chủ động thích ứng với biến đổi khí hậu và bảo đảm an ninh lương thực.

Các chuyên gia quốc tế khẳng định, kỹ thuật chỉnh sửa gen, tiêu biểu là CRISPR/Cas, mang lại bước tiến mang tính cách mạng nhờ khả năng can thiệp chính xác, có chủ đích vào hệ gen mục tiêu mà không đưa vật liệu di truyền ngoại lai vào cơ thể sinh vật. [...] Trong định hướng phát triển khoa học, công nghệ và đổi mới sáng tạo phục vụ tái cơ cấu ngành nông nghiệp, công nghệ sinh học thế hệ mới ngày càng khẳng định vị trí động lực then chốt. Theo Quyết định số 1131/QĐ-TTg của Thủ tướng Chính phủ về Danh mục công nghệ chiến lược và sản phẩm công nghệ chiến lược, công nghệ chỉnh sửa gen thuộc nhóm công nghệ y - sinh học tiên tiến, được định hướng ưu tiên ứng dụng mạnh mẽ trong y tế và nông nghiệp. Những sáng kiến có khả năng nng cao chất lượng sản phẩm, hiệu quả quản lý và năng suất lao động được khuyến khích tham gia.

items.title: Sở Khoa học và Công nghệ Hà Tĩnh hướng dẫn xét công nhận sáng kiến và đánh giá hiệu quả đề tài khoa học
items.summary: Theo hướng dẫn, các giải pháp được xem xét công nhận là sáng kiến bao gồm: giải pháp kỹ thuật, giải pháp quản lý, giải pháp tác nghiệp và giải pháp ứng dụng tiến bộ kỹ thuật. "For mundane intellectual labor, AI is just going to replace everybody"

In 93 seconds, he explains why this time is different: one person with an AI assistant will do the work of 10

The new jobs everyone promises? If AI can do all routine thinking work, he asks what jobs are left to create

Then the part that hits hardest. His niece answers complaint letters for a health service. Each one took her 25 minutes. Now AI writes it, she checks it, and it takes 5. So they need five times fewer of her

He agrees it won't be AI that takes your job, it'll be a person using AI. That just means far fewer people

items.title: Recent Advances in AI Are Creating a ‘Paradigm Shift’ for Robotics | Research UC Berkeley
items.summary:
In recent months, artificial intelligence agents that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped computer coding, online shopping, dinner reservations and cyberattacks.

Robotics might be next.

Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. [...] Then, AI agents generate and connect these skills into a robot program. Using NVIDIA’s Isaac simulation libraries, the agents autonomously rehearse the program across task variations, identify where failures happen and refine the approach before deployment. [...] OpenAI’s recent release of its Astra model made the process even more promising, Goldberg said. His postdoctoral students Eric Kaiyuan Chen and Shuangyu Xie gave Astra access to their simulation interface and a short video of a real robot whose assignment was using a sponge to wipe ink off a metal bar. In less than an hour, the AI tool created and fine-tuned a physics simulation that accurately reproduced the video, including very realistic deformations of the sponge.

items.title: Live online certificate brings AI expertise to finance professionals | Cornell Chronicle
items.summary: That philosophy is reflected in the curriculum, which progresses from AI foundations and tools to financial use cases, responsible AI, industry applications and leadership. Participants examine applications including investment research, credit risk, fraud detection, compliance, client engagement and operational efficiency, while also considering issues such as hallucinations, data security, regulation and governance. The program concludes by asking participants to identify opportunities for AI [...] The AI in Finance certificate, offered through eCornell as a collaboration between the Cornell Duffield College of Engineering and the Cornell SC Johnson College of Business, debuted in spring 2026 with 37 participants. Unlike many online certificate programs built primarily around prerecorded material, the program is taught live online, allowing participants to interact directly with Cornell faculty and industry practitioners. [...] Averbukh, who is also a professor of practice in the School of Operations Research and Information Engineering, said conversations with those practitioners increasingly turned toward artificial intelligence – first big data and predictive analytics, then machine learning and, more recently, generative and agentic AI.

items.title: Google AI policy forces decision for San Diego schools – NBC 7 San Diego
items.summary:
As districts consider their options, students are already seeing artificial intelligence become a more common part of everyday learning.

“I feel like I see a lot of people using AI now,” said Delilah Ortiz, a student at El Camino High School.

Some students believe the focus should be on establishing guidelines for AI use rather than banning the technology entirely. [...] San Diego County school districts face a January deadline to decide whether to opt in to Google's artificial intelligence features or lose access to the company's search engine, forcing educators to weigh the benefits of AI against concerns about student access to the technology. [...] Google plans to disable a range of AI-powered features, including Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search in January to give school districts more control over the technology students can access. However, districts that want to continue using Google Search will have to opt in to the AI features.

The 2026 World Cup brought more than six million spectators from around the world to more than 100 matches in 16 host cities in the U.S., Canada and Mexico over the course of two months, prompting a massive interagency effort to secure those sites using technologies like AI and drones. Two people were charged in connection with another bomb threat against FIFA during a World Cup match at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. The previously undisclosed incident occurred June 18, when Switzerland faced Bosnia and Herzegovina at SoFi Stadium outside Los Angeles, Army Capt. items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary:
Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] Berkeley-based Ambi Robotics, which specializes in logistics and warehouse order fulfillment, applied the new methods earlier this year to analyze parcel sorting data and test updates to robot behavior. Tests showed an increased capacity of over 15,000 packages sorted annually per robot; the change is now deployed across 30% of the company’s U.S. fleet. [...] Ken Goldberg

“Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI Tries to Ease Backlash Against AI Data Centers
items.summary:
OpenAI is promising to pay for the power costs accrued by its data centers and give communities more say over construction. The list of commitments came two days after midterm election results favored candidates that opposed the data center buildout aimed at supporting the growing artificial intelligence industry.

See Also: Frictionless Security: How AI is Redefining Access in Highly Regulated Industries [...] For enterprise technology leaders, the announcements are a mixed bag. OpenAI is attempting to ensure it has access to the compute it will need to grow by assuaging the concerns of communities that are increasingly saying no to data center expansion, but for businesses that are still trying to formulate their AI strategy, OpenAI's compact doesn't offer much certainty. [...] The compact outlined locally tailored agreements for future OpenAI campuses, community input into development plans and annual public progress reports. OpenAI said it will cover the electricity it consumes and the incremental infrastructure costs required to serve its sites. It will also provide financial assurances before major spending begins to protect other utility customers if a project is delayed, reduced or canceled.
